committee_action.meethigh:
The Committee approved to subject HB 4498 to a TWG, with Rep. Jose Enrique Garcia III as chair, and the following as members:  Reps. Rodriguez, Limkaichong, Rodrigo Abellanosa, Acosta, Juliette Uy and Alexandria Gonzales. 
 
	Ms. Roman-Tayag requested that they be invited to the TWG to be able to share the BSPâ€™s experience in the crafting of the legislative measure.   
	
	The Committee likewise approved to consolidate House Bill No. 5540, introduced by Reps. Michael Romero and Enrico Pineda, with HB 4498 because among its provisions are the increase in capitalization of the SB Corp. and the mandatory allocation of credit resources to small enterprises, which are also stipulated in HB 4498, and can likewise be considered as amendments to the Magna Carta for MSMEs.

committee_action.remarks: Consideration and Approval of the Draft Substitute Bill on House Bill No. 4498, introduced by Rep. Maximo B. Rodriguez, Jr.,  and House Bill No. 5540,  introduced by Reps. Michael L. Romero and Enrico A. Pineda, re: Amendments to the Magna Carta for MSMEs
committee_action.meethigh:
Committee Chairman Peter Unabia stated that the approval of the substitute bill, which was reported out by the Technical Working Group (TWG), was deferred during the last committee meeting held on September 26, 2017 for the following reasons:

1.	Awaiting submission of the position paper of the Department of Budget and Management (DBM).
2.	Further review of the Penal Provisions of the proposed substitute bill, together with the IRR of the law on the sanctions.

In its unofficial position on the bill, the DBM representative, Assistant Secretary Grace delos Santos, stated that:

1.	The national government should not incur additional costs for the establishment of a guarantee system for distressed enterprises;
2.	The amount and timeframe in the proposed bill to fully finance the authorized capital of Small Business Corporation (SB Corp.) is not economically practical or efficient stating that the funds may be utilized for other priority programs and projects. The provision of funds for the needs of the MSME sector must be viewed with an expanded timeframe.
3.	Interposed no objection to the establishment of a P500 million Venture Capital Fund, however there is no separate implementing guidelines and selection criteria that must be set-up on the grant of the seed fund. A portion of the income generated from the interest of loans under the SB Corp.â€™s Pondo sa Pagbabago and Pag-Asenso program should be allocated as Venture Capital Fund.
4.	The Committee should request for the comments of the Government Commission for GOCCs (GCG), and the Department of Finance (DOF) with regard to the capitalization requirements of the SB Corp. 

In summary, the DBM is constrained from favorably endorsing the proposed bill in its present form. 

In reaction, Chairman Unabi requested the DBM to review its position, considering President Duterteâ€™s pronouncement in the recent ASEAN Economic Summit  that his administration will strongly support MSMEs, believing that they are the driving force for economic development. Reps. Jose Enrique Garcia III and Jocelyn S. Limkaichong echoed the Presidentâ€™s statement that he will review the budget and increase the allocation for MSMEs.

The Committee approved the following additional amendments to the bill:

1.	Delete the phrase â€œin the amount of Five Hundred Million Pesos (P500,000,000.00)â€� as itemized contribution by the Land Bank of the Philippines (LBP) and the Development Bank of the Philippines (DBP); and
2.	Define the term â€œsmaller banksâ€�, with the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) tasked to craft the language. This is to categorize and differentiate middle banks from small banks and thrift banks.

The Committee approved the substitute bill, subject to amendments, with all the members present even in the past meetings thereon, to be included as co-authors.

committee_action.meethigh:
Philippine Export Confederation, Inc. (PhilExport) and Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) proposed amendments to the substitute bill, which were approved by the Committee.

The Committee approved the substitute bill to House Bills Numbered 4498 and 5540, as amended, subject to style.

Chairman Laogan directed the Secretariat to finalize to the substitute bill; follow-up with the Committee on Appropriations on its action on the funding provisions of the substitute bill; and, after approval by the Committee on Appropriations, to prepare and file the appropriate Committee Report.
